method_reference.citation: Ambure P, Halder AK, Gonzalez-Diaz H, Cordeiro MNDS. QSAR-Co: An Open Source Software for Developing Robust Multitasking or Multitarget Classification-Based QSAR Models. J Chem Inf Model. 2019;59(6):2538-2544. doi:10.1021/acs.jcim.9b00295
method_reference.pagination: Page numbers here are pages of the PDF as pdftotext paginates it: 30 pages, page 1 the cover and page 6 blank (it carries only the Snapshot 2 figure). An earlier reading of the same document in this project paginated it as 29 pages, having dropped that blank page, so its citations run one lower than these from p. 7 onward. The section titles quoted alongside each number identify the passage either way.
method_reference.the_manual_never_defines: r2, q2 (leave-one-out or external), RMSE or MAE appear nowhere in the manual, because QSAR-Co is classification-only. Its validation vocabulary is Wilks lambda, the confusion-matrix metrics, MCC, ROC/AUC, Y-randomisation and the applicability domain. No claim of the form 'QSAR-Co requires q2 above x' could be sourced to it, and none is made here: the continuous statistics in the regression regimes below are the ordinary QSAR ones, used because this repository's Hansch work is regression, and they are labelled as coming from outside the manual.
deviations: The manual's Box-Jenkins operator is not printed in the PDF, so the published deviation-from-condition-mean form is used and labelled as such.
The manual gives one variance cut-off (0.001) without naming the scale; it is applied to descriptors scaled 0-1 so that one cut-off means the same thing for every descriptor.
The manual's F-measure sentence on p. 14 contradicts its own formula; the formula is used, on fractions.

Splitting and cross-validation are grouped by compound, which the manual does not discuss because it assumes one row per compound. This table has one row per drug and mode of administration, so an ungrouped split would put the same molecule in both sets.

measured_activity_merge.status: measured pChEMBL potency merged from the curated drugs.json by PubChem CID
measured_activity_merge.join: PubChem CID only; existing non-empty cells in the primary file are kept

formulas.in_vivo_activity: WHO defined daily dose for the route, in mg, / 70 kg

assumptions: the lethal doses in this group are not one kind of number: ranitidine's and nizatidine's are intravenous LD50s, famotidine's is an oral LD50 given as a lower bound, and cimetidine has no published LD50 at all, only a two-year no-effect dose. A therapeutic index is only comparable between values of the same kind and the same route, so each row carries both.

ranitidine: the lethal dose is the cited intravenous LD50 of 83 mg/kg, not the 77.0 mg/kg the label reader took from the label text, because only the cited value carries the route and species the figure belongs to.
ranitidine bismuth citrate: the PubChem record is a mixture of 3 fragments, so the largest one is taken as the drug, as the curation rules require.
cimetidine, combinations (A02BA51): PubChem has no single compound under this name (a combination or a salt-only entry), so the row is left out of the table.
famotidine, combinations (A02BA53): PubChem has no single compound under this name (a combination or a salt-only entry), so the row is left out of the table.
The primary biological target is taken to be CHEMBL1941 (Histamine H2 receptor): the mechanism target ChEMBL gives for 6 of the 8 members that have a structure.

Hammet Substituent Constant is left empty in every row. A Hammett sigma is defined for a substituent on a fixed parent ring, and the members of this group differ in the ring itself, so no common parent exists and no sigma can be read off a table. Molar refractivity fills the steric half of the same column pair.

Lipophilicity(log D) holds the Crippen log P computed by RDKit, with PubChem's XLogP3 kept beside it. Neither is a log D: a distribution coefficient at pH 7.4 needs each drug's pKa, which none of the sources used here publish.

In Vivo Toxicity(Cell Culture) holds a whole-animal figure, the lowest acute lethal dose in mg/kg stated in the US label text, not a cell-culture figure. The workbook's own formula calls this cell the in-vivo toxicity parameter, and no cell-culture toxicity value for these drugs exists in the open sources used here.

In Vivo Activity(Therapeutic Response) holds the WHO defined daily dose for that route, converted to mg/kg for a 70 kg adult. A DDD is the assumed average maintenance dose for the drug's main indication in adults, so it is a dose that produces the therapeutic response, and the WHO publishes it per route, which is what makes the per-route comparison possible.

Therapeutic Index is computed exactly as the workbook writes it, LOG(toxicity) - LOG(1/activity), which equals log10(toxicity x activity). The conventional index, log10(LD50/ED50), is in its own column. The workbook's form is the right one when the activity cell holds a potency, where bigger means more active; the classical form is the right one when it holds a dose in mg/kg, which is the case here, so the classical column is the one to read.
Dose Interval is 24 hours in every row, because a defined daily dose is one day's dose. A label's own dosing interval would differ by product and strength, and is not comparable across routes.

Bioavailability and half-life are read out of the label prose by pattern, and each row keeps the sentence the number came from so it can be checked. Sentences about renal or hepatic impairment, children and neonates are skipped so the figure is the ordinary adult one.

A drug appears once per mode of administration. Descriptors, structure, target and the in-vitro numbers are properties of the molecule, so they repeat across its route rows; bioavailability, dose and the free concentration are properties of the route, so they differ.

meta.determinism: fixed seed, descriptors recomputed from curated SMILES, rows sorted before use, no timestamps outside this meta block

can_this_data_support_model_selection.wide table (QED-derived labels): yes, for the question it actually asks
can_this_data_support_model_selection.measured-activity table: yes for model selection (308 compounds with a measured potency), with a weak signal expected

why: The A02BA cohort is a handful of compounds. Model selection needs an external set that is itself large enough to separate models; here it is not large enough to separate anything, so the cohort is reported with leave-one-compound-out only and no winner.

The widest table has enough compounds for a genuine external set and a compounds-per-descriptor ratio far above the five-per-term rule, so model selection there is meaningful - but the response is QED, a computed property, not a measured biological one.

The measured-activity table is the only regime with a real biological response and enough compounds to validate on. Its drugs share no target, so a weak result there is the expected result, not a failure of the ladder.
honest_verdict.qsar_co_is_classification_only: QSAR-Co develops and validates two-class models only (manual p. 11-12: two-class LDA and Random Forest). What it validates is therefore a classification restatement of this problem - the response cut at its median - not the continuous Hansch regression. The regression half of this ladder is validated with continuous QSAR statistics instead, and the two halves are ranked separately and never compared to each other.

regimes.label: wide-qed-class [normal]
regimes.description: every curated drug, one row per drug and mode of administration; the response is the QED drug-likeness class
regimes.class_rule: class 1 when QED >= the median, else 0
caveats: QED is a deterministic function of its own eight component properties, so a ladder that is handed those eight back cannot do anything but reproduce them. The descriptor block here deliberately excludes all eight (MW, ALOGP, HBA, HBD, PSA, ROTB, AROM, ALERTS) and their desirabilities, so this is a real generalisation question: how far do descriptors QED does not use predict the QED class.
QED-derived labels are a property of the molecule, not a measured biological response: this regime tests the pipeline and the descriptors, not pharmacology
